NVIDIA Attestation SDK offline collateral test fixtures
Source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/attestation-sdk
Modified source: https://github.com/gkostal/attestation-sdk
License: Apache-2.0 (see accompanying LICENSE).

rubin_vbios_example.cbor and rubin_driver_example.cbor were generated from the
SDK's sample_rims/corim/*.diag examples. They are unsigned test reference values.
rubin-cmw-cert-chain.pem was extracted from sample_attestation_data/rubin_evidence.cmw.json.
The source CMW is unmodified. Its BROM serial is 410a3021db2466fe7c, not the serial
418f2e55a169f0b0e3 in the separate gpu/rubinCertChain.txt sample.

ocsp/*.der are genuine signed GOOD OCSPResponse captures from
https://ocsp.ndis.nvidia.com on 2026-11-13. rubin-metadata.json records the actual
CMW's three lookup keys, validity times and SHA-256 checksums. The additional
response for the separate sample BROM certificate is retained, with its capture
metadata in original-sample-metadata.json. These public certificate status
responses are retained without modification for deterministic offline replay.

test-root.pem, synthetic_evidence.cmw.json, synthetic-good/* and
synthetic-revoked/* are generated test artifacts, NOT NVIDIA production identities.
They retain the CMW's DTI-bearing certificate extensions and measurements, but use
a generated test root, ICA and SPDM-signing leaf and a newly signed transcript.
The revoked leaf response is signed and contains keyCompromise status.
No private keys are retained. The test root must never be trusted in production.
synthetic-metadata.json pins a valid replay time and the test OCSP lookup keys.

Regeneration tools: scripts/capture-rubin-ocsp.sh and
scripts/generate-offline-fixtures.cpp. Tests do not regenerate or fetch fixtures.
